findings.summary: Hestia's self-queued requests are not counted: Hestia queues on channel "cli", not "steward"
findings.evidence: Every production call site where Hestia queues work calls `self.queue(&text)`, which is Athena::queue in reading.rs:962. That is the only `fn queue(` on Athena, and it sets `channel: "cli"`. Only steward.rs RequestQueue (line 676) uses REQUEST_CHANNEL. The real records in the evidence snapshot agree: Hestia root-cause requests 20261109-090843-mc8v, 20261111-145400-dx3z and 20261114-045630-wqa6 all have `"channel": "cli"`. The request asked for 'steward and Hestia requests', and the accepted reading told the producer to confirm Hestia's channel and include it if it differs. As written, the line leaves out every Hestia fix, so a stuck Hestia backlog stays invisible. Correct alternatives: either have Hestia record its own channel (for example a distinct channel that is also drained) and count it, or identify Hestia requests from data already recorded. If either is out of scope, report the gap instead of claiming coverage.

findings.summary: The doc comment and the CHANGELOG claim that Hestia uses the steward channel, which the code contradicts
findings.evidence: The doc comment reads 'channel REQUEST_CHANNEL, which the steward and Hestia both use', and the CHANGELOG says 'steward::REQUEST_CHANNEL, which Hestia requests also use'. Both are false per reading.rs:980 and the hestia.rs call sites above.

findings.summary: A changed file is outside the expected deliverables
findings.evidence: The deliverables list status.rs, CHANGELOG.md, steward.rs, docs/design/hestia.md and athena-cli/src/main.rs. The diff changes crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs, which is where status text is actually rendered. The edit is necessary, but it is not on the list.

findings.summary: 'run' includes requests closed without ever running
findings.evidence: Any state other than Queued, Proposed or Declined counts as run, so Closed(Dropped), Closed(Stale) and Closed(Abandoned) count too. A backlog cleared by dropping or staling requests would show as 'run'. The accepted reading allows this ('terminal outcome such as ... closed'), but a separate 'closed unrun' count would describe the backlog more truthfully.

findings.summary: No test covers the display wiring
findings.evidence: The tests check SelfQueued::text only. No test shows that `athena status` output contains the line. `status --snapshot` prints only the job, history and throughput sections, so I could not observe the line against real records.

summary: The change adds a `self-queued fixes  last 7d: N queued, M run · total: N queued, M run` line to `athena status`. The line is computed in `SelfQueued` (status.rs) and printed from display.rs. Its three new unit tests pass under `cargo test -p athena-core status`, and the recorded fmt, clippy and test checks passed. However, the line does not count Hestia's requests, and the request named those explicitly ("steward and Hestia requests"). Every production call site where Hestia queues work (spec_review, the repeated-cause backfill and requeue, and design and gate requests) uses `Athena::queue` (reading.rs:962). That function writes `channel: "cli"`. The evidence snapshot agrees: Hestia's "Fix the root cause of a repeated failure" requests, such as 20261109-090843-mc8v, 20261111-145400-dx3z and 20261114-045630-wqa6, are all on channel "cli". The accepted reading assumed Hestia shares the steward channel but told the producer to confirm this in hestia* and to include Hestia's channel if it differs. The producer did not do that check. Instead, the doc comment and the CHANGELOG entry state as fact that Hestia uses the steward channel, which is false. So the owner's backlog line leaves out a whole class of self-queued fixes and documents that wrongly. Because of this, the verdict is fail even though each criterion is met as worded. There are also two smaller issues. First, display.rs is changed although it is not on the deliverables list. Second, requests closed without running, such as dropped or stale ones, count as "run".
